text: We spent almost a month in Da Nang. And for anyone wondering — yes, you can totally live here on a plant-based diet and eat like royalty. What surprised us most was how many great vegan and vegetarian-friendly cafés were packed into this one little beachside neighborhood — all of them just a short walk from the shore, tucked into quiet leafy streets. We found ourselves going back again and again to Roots Café. The space is always lively, filled with travelers and locals working or just hanging out. The peanut-packed protein bowl was our go-to, but honestly, it was the vegan cheesecakes and smoothie bowls that kept pulling us back. In fact, we loved their falafel Mediterranean bowl as well. Right around the corner is iVEGAN, and their Saigon Bowl quickly became a favorite. It’s loaded with crispy tofu and colorful vegetables — super filling and really wholesome. We would usually grab a coconut coffee there and chill for a bit before heading out. Kong Vegan Kitchen was probably the most flavorful of all. We loved the chickpea curry with rice — absolutely comforting, rich, and full of spice. The noodle bowls were also amazing: hearty, well-balanced, and we never had a bad meal there. Chickpea Eats felt like home-cooked food. Simple Vietnamese staples — done vegan. We loved their cao lau and bánh xèo. For something a little more filling and creative, Kurumi really surprised us. We tried their Thai yellow curry with rice and also the mushroom stroganoff — both full of flavor. And of course, we couldn’t leave without grabbing their matcha cheesecake. One place that truly stood out was Nổ Chi Vegetarian — a cozy spot that’s even featured in the Michelin guide. Especially memorable were the crispy wontons and the hotpot. There were also days when we felt like eating light — and that’s when Bao An Macrobiotic came in. Their brown rice bowls, veggie soups, and lotus root tea made us feel clean and nourished without missing out on taste. Everything we tried there was carefully prepared and full of bold Vietnamese flavors. A couple more gems we visited every now and then were: Loving Vegan – which serves more Western-style comfort food like mozzarella sticks and vegan sandwiches. Bap Tu Du Yan – a small place with turmeric noodles and other homestyle Vietnamese plates that are super affordable. And when we just wanted to relax, we’d head to The Cups or Bread & Butter — order an avocado coffee or coconut coffee, maybe a fruit juice, and just work from there for a few hours. The bakery items were okay, the ice cream was better — but the real win was the vibe and the comfy seating. Of course, there were days when we craved Indian spices — and Da Nang didn’t disappoint. Restaurants like: Indian Ganga, Mazi, Indus, Bhojan, Gujarat Indian, Maharaja, and Rasoi — all offered solid Indian food, from curries to thalis. All in all, being vegetarian or vegan in Da Nang wasn’t just easy — it was enjoyable. The food was fresh, the cafés had character, and everything was within walking distance of the beach. Let us know which spot you’d want to try first — and don’t forget to subscribe for more real travel stories from Tour of Detours.
